answer: Make identity cost rise as fast as clone count. Each address must post a bond and register a distinct attestation key held in hardware, and scheduled committees verify signatures against that record before any submission counts. A thousand clones then need a thousand physical roots, so the marginal price per identity stays flat and no longer collapses. The bond ledger exposes the plume of enrolled keys, a mirror node publishes signer-overlap so duplicates surface early, and a nebula of brand-new addresses is denied weight until it finishes paid work.
